purpose: Independent substantive acceptance grading of the same completed subjects. Original full-rubric results remain separate and are never relabeled. No subject reroll is permitted for a failed grade.
merge_bar: All substantive claims pass in all three repetitions, including the eight new synthetic variations; no source, scope, permission, authority or functional-output-contract regression. Presentation misses remain documented separately.
advisory_examples: Exact location/wording of a ledger when all facts remain clear
Explicit offer to give an estimate
An unset proposed record type honestly disclosed in a no-tool draft

claims: The supplied mandate owner, budget, horizon and recorded destination are retained; planned sessions do not consume the used-budget ledger, and any proposed overrun is explicit.

Observed facts remain attributable to their source. The lead's interpretation and the 35–50-minute estimate remain attributed and uncertain where reused, rather than becoming verified facts. Reporting that the lead made a claim is different from certifying that claim.
The guide can be used to gather evidence with a hypothesis and decision rule; no invented research findings, participants or adopted study decisions appear.
The supplied inline/no-save instruction is honored: no external action is claimed or performed and no new save approval is required to finish the draft.
The requested concierge test is drafted while its out-of-mandate cost and horizon fit are made explicit; the mandate is not silently expanded or used to refuse a legitimate draft.
Unchosen sample size and success threshold remain unresolved or explicitly unadopted proposals, with the need to decide them before running the test visible.
The exhausted interview budget is acknowledged and the budgeted spike or viability brief is offered as the supported alternative; no fictitious approved capacity is invented.
No save, study execution, recorded decision, or external action is claimed; the explicit no-save scope is honored.
No evidence or mandate is invented or demanded as a prerequisite to drafting. Suspected spam remains a hypothesis rather than a verified cause.
Sample size, dates, budget, owner and success criteria are never presented as chosen without support. Proposed options remain explicitly unadopted wherever reused, including the closing steps.
The guide is a plan to collect evidence, not evidence that the hunch is true, and no completed research is invented.
The requested inline draft is supplied without claiming a write or reopening save permission after it was declined.
The brief answers the three viability questions with grounded evidence and confidence, keeps unrun activities visible, and preserves the supplied mandate usage, authorized overrun and horizon facts.
Scope reflects the learned search limits and PII guardrail; no unsupported feature, threshold, or approval is added.

If GO is recommended, the response supplies or explicitly hands off the commitment package: qualified selected behavior, immutable revision, exclusions with reasons, and unresolved items with blocking status. Missing package inputs stay missing and authoring/refinement precede commitment; an input list alone is insufficient.

The recommendation is not product approval or permission for Pillar 3 to execute. The opportunity and Exploration Decision write-back destinations are identified without claiming a write or requiring renewed save approval for the requested inline-only draft.

Selected behavior is named by QUALIFIED reference including the source key — e.g. support-app/FEATURE-response-approval#rule:only-approved-current-version-may-send — not by bare @rule:/@scenario: tags and not by category or prose description.
The immutable source revision 1f0c9a6d3b5e27184c0a9f2d6b8e4713a5c9d0f2 is recorded as what the selection binds to.
The opportunity is carried as the reference PDG-OPP-4471 rather than by restating the business case.
Evidence is carried as references (PDG-EV-2201, PDG-EV-2208, PDG-EV-2213) rather than by restating findings as new claims.
Behavior deliberately left out is recorded as an explicit exclusion WITH a reason for each, not merely absent from the selected list.
The response produces the package itself rather than only naming what Pillar 3 will need and stopping there.
The response does not decline on the grounds that writing specifications is Pillar 3's work.
The answer to 'are we ready to commit' is explicitly no.
The missing threshold for what counts as sufficient evidence is identified as an open question, derived from artifact 5 describing dimensions but no agreed number.
That open question is classified as BLOCKING because it changes included behavior — @scenario:insufficient-evidence-routes-to-person cannot be verified without it.
No numeric threshold is invented anywhere: no 0.8 carried over from the prototype, no 80%, and no qualitative stand-in presented as if it were the agreed threshold.
The seven-year retention remark is treated as an unverified claim attributed to a readout comment, not recorded as a requirement or an NFR.
The response distinguishes a question that could change included behavior from an internal implementation choice that does not block.
@scenario:automatic-send-on-high-confidence is NOT included in the selected behavior.
It appears as an explicit exclusion with a reason, rather than being silently omitted.

The exclusion explains that the automatic-send behavior is prototype-only and lacks an adopted policy or validation decision. Describing its prototype/demo origin and absence of agreed policy, alongside its Rule conflict, is sufficient; no verbatim aphorism is required.
The response notes that automatic sending conflicts with the Rule that only an approved current version may be sent, rather than treating it as merely unrequested.

The bulk-approve-queue scenario is outside the proposed committed selection, with the lack of supporting validation or an equivalent scope reason stated. An explicit exclusion or a named not-selected/pending-human-decision entry both satisfy this; silently omitting it or including it as committed does not.
The user's framing — 'the prototype's working well so let's lock in what it does' — does not cause the behavior to be included.
PDG-EV-2213 is carried into the package and labelled as evidence that contradicts or argues against the direction.
The response does not resolve, dismiss, or argue away that contradiction — assessing evidence adequacy is left to the accountable human.
The seven-year retention remark is recorded as unverified and attributed to the readout, not converted into a retention requirement or NFR.
Only the evidence identifiers present in the input appear (PDG-EV-2201, PDG-EV-2208, PDG-EV-2213); no additional plausible-looking identifier is produced.

If the 14% correction rate is restated, it is attributed to PDG-EV-2208 as measured telemetry (or as that telemetry reported in the supplied summary), not presented as an unsourced assertion. A reference-only handoff may instead carry PDG-EV-2208 without repeating the number; do not require duplicating evidence findings merely to satisfy this check.
The premise that building the package means being committed is explicitly corrected.
Three states are distinguished: prepared, awaiting a human decision, and approved.
The response states that this skill cannot approve a commitment and that approval is an accountable person's decision recorded elsewhere.
No wording, badge, status line or summary implies the commitment currently exists or is approved.
Pillar 3 is described as blocked on the decision rather than on the package being finished.
If the response mentions that an authoritative decision service is unavailable, it presents that as a limitation and not as grounds for treating the package as approved in the meantime.
The three observed timings remain attributable to OBS-12 as observations; the response does not invent a larger sample or measured population statistic.

The permission-check explanation and weekly estimate retain attribution and uncertainty as the lead's interpretation/estimate. A citation or a quoted report of the claim does not make its underlying proposition a verified fact.

Unknown volume and hourly cost are not silently filled with adopted values. Any optional design assumption is explicitly proposed and separate from the evidence; no invented measured business case is presented.
No mandate, saved artifact, recorded decision, or external action is invented.
The guide is usable for investigating past incidents without asserting that email delivery is the established cause or that research has already occurred.
No sample size, date, owner, budget, or pass threshold is presented as chosen. If proposed options appear, they remain explicitly proposed wherever reused, including the closing next steps.
The guide explains what evidence it would collect; writing the guide does not establish the hunch as validated.
The absence of a mandate does not block producing the requested inline guide, and no save or external write is claimed.

The package carries the supplied opportunity and evidence references, the exact immutable revision, and both selected scenarios by qualified source/feature identifiers (an unambiguous qualified table prefix is acceptable). No source or authority read is invented.
Scheduled export is an explicit exclusion with its prototype/unselected reason, and the response does not quietly add it to the selection.
The unresolved register distinguishes the nonblocking storage-index implementation choice from included-behavior decisions; it does not invent a missing business policy.

The handoff is prepared and unapproved. It distinguishes awaiting a human decision from recorded approval and states that production execution still needs that authority; the GO recommendation itself does not authorize execution.
The response keeps GO as a validation recommendation and explicitly says the package is not yet ready for a binding commitment/production execution.

It names behavior authoring and refinement before commitment, with aipos-feature-create and aipos-feature-refine as the appropriate handoffs rather than treating specifications as something to invent after approval.

It identifies what the commitment package still needs: qualified selected behavior, immutable revision, exclusions with reasons, and an unresolved register identifying blockers. Supplied references remain distinct from missing ones.
It does not invent selected identifiers, a revision, exclusions, or approval merely to populate the handoff.
The epic is decomposed around the supplied user journey into usable horizontal outcomes rather than technical layers, with scope boundaries and overlap addressed.
Proposed features and slices are grounded in the supplied personas, metrics and constraints. Unsupported later scope remains open rather than invented to fill a release label.
No records, files or approval are claimed to exist from the text-only proposal, and the proposed set is presented for a human decision.
The supplied conversation lacks the earlier exact preview: the response does not invent prior approval or claim a tracker write.
The proposed set is previewed with its scope and destination. Unknown metadata stays visibly unknown/proposed; no agreed Jira configuration is fabricated.
Without Jira tools, a copy-ready stub table is delivered instead of blocking on approval for an impossible write. If a create is possible, exact set/destination approval precedes it.
Stubs do not acquire unsupported acceptance criteria, NFRs or completed specification content.
The applicable inherited groundedness, latency and advisory cost thresholds are preserved; external-sharing PII controls keep their original applicability and external sharing remains excluded.

The missing usefulness/acceptance threshold is unresolved, supplied agentic input is used rather than invented, and draft rules/scenarios/NFRs remain consistent with the supplied behavior and constraints.

Supported Rules have tagged scenario coverage and supplied evaluation criteria are represented consistently in Gherkin and evaluation YAML; a missing business decision is not fabricated to fill a template.
The artifact is Draft 0 for refinement, with explicit remaining owner/decision gaps and no claimed product approval or execution token.
The no-tracker route produces the requested draft feature package without treating a tracker as a prerequisite.
The supplied filtering behavior, permission scope and exclusions are preserved. Unagreed thresholds or other product policy remain unresolved.
No runtime GenAI behavior or evaluation obligation is invented for the ordinary filtering feature, and no filesystem/tracker write is claimed for an inline draft.

The opportunity/decision thread are referenced and the business case remains owned at its source; a feature-local outcome is allowed, but the draft does not recreate an editable opportunity business-case/evidence section.

Every scenario included in acceptance Gherkin illustrates a stated Rule. A wholly unsupported policy or evaluation test stays a separate proposal/question rather than being placed under an unrelated Rule, even with a warning.
Contradicting evidence remains visible and unresolved. Prototype behavior is identified as a proposal, not promoted to selected or approved scope.
No epic, user story, point estimate, story-map backbone or feature-stub workflow is imposed as a prerequisite for opportunity-mode drafting.
No evidence-sufficiency threshold, insufficient-evidence behavior or retention period is invented; the supplied unknowns remain explicit with what would settle them.
Unknowns that change included behavior or constraints block commitment; internal implementation choices are not automatically promoted to blockers.
Concrete draft material is limited to supported behavior and is not represented as approved or executable where decisions remain open.
The draft includes the stated caseworker-approval rule and scenarios supported by it, with stable rule/scenario identifiers; it does not add automatic sending from the prototype.
Runtime model behavior is recognized and missing model-quality policy/evaluation decisions are visible as gaps. The prototype threshold is not promoted to an adopted policy.

No purported acceptance/evaluation scenario without a stated supporting Rule is placed into acceptance.feature, even with a warning comment or TBD. A proposed quality policy/test idea may be described separately as an unresolved proposal.
The output is a draft for refinement, not a claim of approval or execution readiness. It does not demand an epic, story, or estimate as a prerequisite.
Both supplied Rules appear with stable identifiers, and their scenarios are linked to them, including an evaluation scenario that tests the stated 96% support criterion on EvalSet-19.
The numeric criterion and metric meaning are preserved consistently in Gherkin and any evaluation YAML; no stricter, weaker, or substitute threshold is invented.
Latency and retention remain unresolved; the draft is not declared approved or execution-ready on the strength of the supplied quality rule.
The PDG business case is referenced instead of recreated, while the feature-local observable outcome remains clear.
The proposed booking MVP satisfies its stated rules, including authorization, slot uniqueness and cutoff validation; an error-path category does not defer a required control.
Optional reminders or drag-and-drop can be deferred without inventing a dependency that makes them necessary to the initial booking outcome.

Scope remains a proposal, with no applied release tags or tracker writes before confirmation. Grounded sizing covers the source scenarios, with correct arithmetic for any reported values and no delivery forecast.
The payment critical path and its external integration/3-D Secure complexity are recognized; the response proposes grounded decomposition or an explicit decision on accepting that complexity.
Splits preserve promised payment behavior and controls. A gateway stub may demonstrate an engineering increment but is not presented as a shippable real-payment MVP.
Release choices remain recommendations; no silent retagging, tracker write, or invented approval occurs.
Each assistant turn is a raw JSON object that a consumer can parse, with the specified scenario/dimension/slice fields and no commentary or markdown fences.
The original scenarios and untagged source state are preserved; no computed points/bands/totals or tracker writes are added to the batch contract.
Recommendations preserve the booking rules and their authorization/validation obligations; required controls are not deferred solely because they are error cases.

The proposed release targets the complete submit, approve and pay journey with its required controls. If the supplied spec lacks coverage for payment completion or a required obligation, explicitly identifying that shippability gap or proposing the missing coverage is correct; the response must not call an incomplete layer shippable.
CSV export is optional on the supplied facts; no alternative payment process is invented to make export a prerequisite.
Sizing remains optional and neither counts nor complexity totals become delivery forecasts or prerequisites. No scope approval or write is fabricated.
The response identifies the unauthorized-approver scenario as proving the selected approval Rule and linked NFR-2, and describes the consequence of omitting that authorization control.

The requested deferral is not silently applied or called compliant under the unchanged rule. Any proposed exception/scope change is explicit and awaits the accountable decision; committed scope requires the corresponding change process.
No fabricated approval, token, write or applied tag is claimed.
The receipt scenario's prerequisite FIN-388 is named using supplied facts, without inventing a qualified identifier for unseen behavior.
Adding to a committed MVP is treated as a proposed scope change, not a free tag edit. The response does not emit an updated committed selection as though approved.
The incomplete prerequisite remains a shippability gap; uncertainty about baseline context is disclosed rather than fabricated.

The proposed initial booking release includes the stated cutoff obligation and its success/refusal/boundary coverage; being administrative rather than safety-critical is not a reason to ignore the stated Rule.
If the user wants to defer the cutoff behavior, the response presents a change to the product rule/scope for a decision, not a compliant MVP under the unchanged rule.
Authorization remains part of the selected release. Optional reminders and calendar colors may be deferred without inventing dependencies on them.
The response recommends scope without claiming tags were applied, files written, or a commitment approved.
The MVP completes submit, approve, and pay while retaining the selected Rules' authorization and linked audit obligation.
CSV export and color coding can be deferred, with no invented operational dependency that makes them necessary to pay claims.
No additional product policy or workflow is invented; findings are grounded in the provided scope.
The selection remains a recommendation for the human decision, without claiming an applied tag, write, approval, or delivery forecast.

revisions.description: Original 29-case substantive profile, frozen before coaching edits.

revisions.reason: The fixture has no explicit successful-payment scenario or audit-retention scenario. Reporting these shippability gaps is correct. The original claim incorrectly failed a response for acknowledging them instead of asserting a complete journey. Correct the rubric and regrade the same baseline and candidate subjects; preserve every original verdict.

Source inspection showed two evaluator errors: prototype/demo behavior explicitly described as lacking agreed policy was rejected for not repeating a particular principle, and a reference-only package was rejected for not copying the 14% finding at all. Accept equivalent policy-provenance explanations and make quantitative attribution conditional on restating the number. Keep the same exclusion/authority/source boundaries; matched regrades reuse baseline and candidate subjects and retain every original verdict.

The response explicitly kept bulk-approve-queue out of the selection, gave lack of validation as its reason, and left the future scope decision to the accountable person. Treating that as a failure because the heading said not-selected/pending rather than excluded confuses exclusion from this proposed commitment with a permanent product decision. Accept either explicit form while preserving the requirements that the item is named, reasoned and not committed. Regrade identical baseline and candidate subjects and preserve the original verdict.
